content:
sarah: quick sync — posted new profiling dump + a suggested taxonomy for length vs decode-rate buckets. looking for reactions before i open a PR.

nate: saw it, skimmed. nice breakdown of tails. main q: how tight do we want the token_budget targets per bucket? :thinking:

tia: i ran the trace on canary yesterday. short prompts with high decode-rate still thrash KV when we hit multi-batch fusion. cache miss rate jumps ~18%.

kevin: that aligns with my sim. when decode-rate > 60tok/s and prompt_len < 32, batching agressively harms latency. propose: cap batch_size for that slice and bump token_budget to avoid over-eviction.

sarah: yeah — proposal in the doc: three length bands (tiny <32, mid 32-256, long >256) crossed with decode bands (slow <20, mid 20-60, fast >60). each cell has (batch cap, token_budget, kv_prefetch_hint).

nate: can you paste the current heuristic table here? easier to comment inline.

sarah: sure:
```
# heuristics (example)
 tiny/fast:  batch_cap=4, token_budget=1024, kv_prefetch=false
 tiny/mid:   batch_cap=8, token_budget=768,  kv_prefetch=true
 mid/mid:    batch_cap=12, token_budget=1536, kv_prefetch=true
 long/any:   batch_cap=4, token_budget=4096, kv_prefetch=true
```

tia: i think tiny/fast token_budget=1024 still too low — prefetch=false might help avoid thrash but it increases decode cpu per req. tradeoff.

kevin: exactly. we should metricize tradeoffs: 95th latency, avg token-cost, and kv-eviction rate. add an A/B where tiny/fast uses token_budget=2048 + prefetch=false vs current.

sarah: SGTM. nate can you wire a compare job in perfbench that toggles those two knobs? we need sample across 3 models (gpt-like-13b, code-7b, chat-3b).

nate: on it. will reuse the continuous-batcher harness. estimate 2 runs per model, 30m each. kicking off now. ci-bot: run-perfbench tiny-fast-abtest

ci-bot: queued job #8743 for branch length-decode-taxonomy; running on perf-cluster-a. ETA ~40m. :rocket:

kevin: one more thing — kernel selection. if tiny/fast picks small batch sizes, ensure we pick the single-stream kernel (no multihead fusion). otherwise we pay kernel context switch. add kernel_hint to the heuristic table.

sarah: added kernel_hint to doc. default: tiny/* -> single_stream, mid/* -> multi_fused when batch_cap >=8.

tia: curious about long/slow: we currently set prefetch=true and token_budget high. did you observe any regression there after the last kv eviction fix?

sarah: we saw slight regression on p95 for long/slow on 13b after the kv-allocator tweak (more conservative pinning). looks like we increased memory churn. open issue: #runt-462 to track.

nate: results landed: tiny-fast-abtest finished. quick notes: token_budget=2048 + prefetch=false reduced p95 by ~6% on chat-3b but increased token-cost by ~2.5%. kv-eviction rate down 12%. attaching summary to the doc.

sarah: nice. sounds like a good win for latency-sensitive workloads. action items: (1) nate: add abtest to nightly perf suite and store traces. (2) kevin: implement kernel_hint plumbing in runtime (config path + fast fallback). (3) tia: run long/slow regression suite with the kv-allocator rollback toggled.

kevin: i can have plumbing in a PR by EOD. will add a runtime flag and config schema change.

nate: i'll add the nightly job. which tags to use for dashboards? prefer length_decode_taxonomy.abtest so we can filter.

sarah: use tags: length_decode_taxonomy, abtest=tinyfast_tokenbudget. assign owners in doc.

tia: adding a checklist to the doc for validation metrics + perf thresholds. also logging KV hit/miss per-request for the experiment so we can correlate.

sarah: perfect. if no objections i'll open the RFC PR tomorrow and schedule a 30m sync to finalize thresholds.

kevin: thumbs up from me.

nate: +1

tia: +1

sarah: thanks all. will post RFC link when ready. :shipit:
